questions.text_english:
(1) As a young adult, life can be stressful and overwhelming at times. Juggling among school, work, social life, and other responsibilities, it can be easy to feel alone and disconnected from the world around us. Dogs are the ultimate companions for anyone looking to alleviate stress and loneliness. We'll explore many reasons why dogs make the best companions for young adults.

(2) Unconditional love: Dogs are known for their loyalty and love for their owners, no matter what. They don't judge us, criticize us, or hold grudges against us. No matter how flawed or imperfect we may be, our dogs will always love us unconditionally. This kind of unwavering support and affection can be incredibly comforting for young adults struggling to find their place in the world.

(3) Social connection: Dogs are great ice-breakers and conversation starters. Whether you're walking them in the park, taking them to the dog beach, or simply hanging out at home, dogs have a way of bringing people together. For young adults who may feel isolated or disconnected from their peers, having a dog by their side can be a great way to connect with others and form new friendships.

(4) Increase physical activity: Dogs require regular exercise in order to stay healthy and happy. This means that young adults who own dogs are more likely to engage in physical activity themselves. Whether its going for a run, playing frisbee, or simply taking a leisurely stroll, getting out with your dog can be a great way to boost your mood and energy levels.

(5) Emotional support: Dogs are also great emotional support animals for those struggling with mental health issues such as anxiety and depression. Their presence alone can provide a sense of calm and comfort, and their ability to sense their owner's emotions can be incredibly comforting. For young adults dealing with mental health challenges, having a dog as a companion can be a life-changing experience.

(6) Improve responsibility and self-care: Owning a dog also comes with a great deal of responsibility and self-care. Dogs require regular feeding, grooming, exercise, and attention, which can be a great way for young adults to develop a sense of responsibility and self-discipline. Additionally, having a dog as a companion can encourage young adults to take better care of themselves, such as making sure they get enough sleep, eat healthy, and engage in regular exercise.

(7) For all these reasons and more, dogs make fantastic companions for young adults. Whether you're looking for emotional support, social connection, increased physical activity, or simply someone to love and be loved by, a dog can provide all these things and more. So the next time you're feeling stressed or overwhelmed, consider finding a furry friend to take on the world with you.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer the following questions, based on the above passage:

sub_questions.text_english: What is the significance of owning a dog for a young adult who is striving for acceptance in society?

options_english.B: It builds a sense of responsibility.
options_english.C: It helps young adults get more sleep.
options_english.D: It is a source of unconditional love.

sub_questions.solution: The passage mentions that for young adults struggling to find their place in the world, the unwavering support and unconditional love of a dog provide comfort and acceptance. While other options are benefits, the emotional assurance of being loved unconditionally directly addresses the need for acceptance.

sub_questions.text_english: A dog can encourage its owner to lead a healthier life by _______ Complete the above sentence appropriately, in about 40 words.
sub_questions.solution: A dog can encourage its owner to lead a healthier life by requiring regular exercise, grooming, and feeding. This forces the owner to stay active, get more sleep, and eat healthier, ultimately fostering self-discipline and better overall self-care habits.

sub_questions.text_english: Share evidence from the text, in approximately 40 words, to support the view that dogs provide a sense of calm and comfort to those struggling with mental health issues.
sub_questions.solution: The text states that dogs act as emotional support animals, helping those with anxiety and depression. Their mere presence provides a sense of calm, and their unique ability to sense their owner's emotions offers profound comfort, making them life-changing companions.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain in about 40 words the statement that 'dogs are great ice-breakers'.
sub_questions.solution: Dogs are 'ice-breakers' because they naturally draw people together, whether at parks, beaches, or even at home. They facilitate social interaction and communication, helping young adults who feel isolated to easily connect with others and initiate new friendships.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following activities help(s) young adults, owning a dog, build their sense of responsibility and self-discipline?

options_english.C: engaging the services of a dog trainer

sub_questions.solution: The passage lists regular feeding, grooming, and exercise as requirements for dog ownership that foster responsibility and self-discipline. Therefore, both walking the dog and feeding it are essential contributing activities.

sub_questions.text_english: What does this article aim to do?

options_english.A: Explain the benefits of owning a dog.
options_english.B: Provide advice on how to get a dog.
options_english.C: Discuss how to take proper care of a dog.
options_english.D: Describe the experiences of dog owners.

sub_questions.solution: The article explicitly states it will 'explore many reasons why dogs make the best companions for young adults', thereby aiming to explain the benefits of dog ownership.

sub_questions.text_english: Select the option that is similar in meaning to the phrase 'take on the world'.
sub_questions.solution: In the context of the passage, 'taking on the world' means facing life's challenges and responsibilities, which aligns with 'accept a responsibility'.

sub_questions.text_english: What does the underlined part in the sentence consider finding a furry friend to take on the world with yourefer to?
sub_questions.solution: The 'furry friend' refers to a dog, which the article presents as an ideal companion for young adults.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the tone of the article?
sub_questions.solution: The article presents the benefits of owning a dog in a constructive, encouraging manner, making the tone positive and informative.

questions.text_english:
(1) A recent survey conducted by an independent research firm sought to measure levels of happiness among youth aged 16-24 years in seven countries. The findings revealed some intriguing insights into what makes today's youth happiest, as well as which factors influence their overall well-being. In India, an overwhelming majority of the youth reported feeling satisfied with their lives, with 87% rating of their overall happiness as 'high' or 'very high.' Financial security was identified as the primary source of happiness for 66%, followed by family support (89%), having a purpose in life (50%), and work or studies (40%). Unfortunately, 65% reported feeling stress related to academic performance or workload, while 25% reported feeling lonely. These figures point to a need for increased mental health support among India's youth.

(2) These surveys also revealed that family support is an important source of contentment for young people across countries. In Europe, 59% of respondents said that their families were a major source of happiness; in France this figure was 67%, and 63% in Germany. In North America, 64% rated family as an important factor for well-being in Canada, while 61% did so in the United States. Similarly, 89% of survey respondents in India named family support as a major contributor to their overall contentment level.

(3) It is clear that stress has a significant impact on the happiness of today's youth. The findings suggest that young people need better resources to manage their mental health and well-being. This may include access to counselling services, mindfulness activities and support groups to help them cope with challenging circumstances. It is also important to provide financial support so as to reduce some of the economic pressures.

(4) In India, 65% of youth surveyed reported feeling anxious about their academic performance or workload, while 25% felt lonely. These figures are especially significant given how important family support is for young people's overall contentment.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer the following questions, based on the above passage:

sub_questions.text_english: What are the two findings that the survey mentioned in paragraph 1 reveals? Answer in about 40 words.
sub_questions.solution: The survey reveals that 87% of Indian youth rate their happiness as high or very high, showing significant life satisfaction. It also identifies key factors influencing their well-being, such as financial security, family support, purpose in life, and work or academic studies.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain in about 40 words the statement It is also important to provide financial support so as to reduce some of the economic pressures.
sub_questions.solution: Since financial security is identified as the primary source of happiness for 66% of Indian youth, providing financial assistance is essential. Reducing economic pressures helps alleviate the stress associated with daily living, thereby improving the overall mental health and well-being of young people.

sub_questions.text_english: Elaborate giving data, the statement Stress has a significant impact on the happiness of today's youth.

key_points: 65% of Indian youth report stress from academic performance, and 25% feel lonely.

sub_questions.solution: The significant impact of stress is confirmed by data showing that 65% of Indian youth experience anxiety due to academic performance or workload, while 25% report feeling lonely.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following factors, with reference to the given passage, does not play a substantial role in the well-being of Indian youth?
sub_questions.solution: The passage highlights family support, social connections, and economic stability (financial security) as factors, but it makes no mention of books and literature as significant contributors.

sub_questions.text_english: State whether True or False, with reference to the given passage: It is not necessary to provide financial support to the youth as only academic performance plays an upper hand in deciding the stress level.
sub_questions.solution: The statement is false because the passage explicitly recommends providing financial support to reduce economic pressures, acknowledging them alongside academic stress.

sub_questions.text_english: What are the top choices which are of maximum value to today's youth?
sub_questions.solution: The passage implies that collectivism (often related to family support) and family ties are of maximum value, as evidenced by 89% of respondents naming family support as a major contributor to their contentment.

sub_questions.text_english: The mental health of today's youth can be managed by resources like _______ and _______
sub_questions.solution: The passage suggests that young people need resources to manage their mental health, such as access to counselling services, mindfulness activities, and support groups.

sub_questions.text_english: Write the following sources that provide happiness to today's youth in descending order : (a) purposefulness (b) financial status (c) family support (d) stress
sub_questions.solution: The descending order of happiness sources is: family support (89%), financial status (66%), and purposefulness (50%). Stress is not a source of happiness.

sub_questions.text_english: You are Priti/Pramod Vats, a resident of 317, Rajdhani Enclave, Rajbagh. You saw the given advertisement in the newspaper and wished to apply for the same. Write a letter to the Personnel Manager along with your bio-data, expressing your interest in the advertised post.
sub_questions.solution: 317, Rajdhani Enclave, Rajbagh. June 5, 2026. The Personnel Manager, Harrison & Simpson Ltd. Subject: Application for the position of Marketing Executive. Dear Sir/Madam, With reference to your advertisement in the newspaper for college graduates for your new cosmetic range, 'I Wish', I am keen to apply. sub_questions.text_english: You have been making documentaries on how rivers, the lifelines of our nation, are under serious threat due to river pollution. Write a letter to the editor of a national daily, examining the reasons for this pollution and suggesting ways of tackling the issue.
sub_questions.solution: To the Editor, National Daily. Subject: Urgent need to address river pollution. Dear Sir/Madam, As a documentary filmmaker focused on our nation's rivers, I am deeply concerned by the alarming levels of pollution. Rivers are under severe threat from untreated industrial waste, agricultural runoff, and human sewage. These toxins are destroying our lifelines. To combat this, we must enforce strict environmental laws and establish monitoring committees to oversee industrial waste disposal. Additionally, we need to modernize our waste handling processes and conduct awareness campaigns to educate the masses on the importance of keeping rivers clean. Immediate collective action is necessary to preserve these precious water bodies for future generations. I hope my concerns reach the authorities through your esteemed newspaper. Yours truly, Srishti/Suraj.

sub_questions.text_english: With rapid digitalization, students have started depending on digital devices for entertainment. This has impacted their lives, both positively and negatively. Write an article with the help of the given cues and your own ideas, highlighting the advantages and disadvantages of using digital devices. You are Rohini/Rohit.
sub_questions.solution: Digital Devices and Children: A Double-Edged Sword. By Rohini/Rohit. In the age of rapid digitalization, children are increasingly dependent on digital devices. While these tools offer significant advantages, such as enhancing academic research, fostering visual intelligence, and improving psychomotor skills, they also present serious downsides. Excessive screen time leads to physical inactivity, poor interpersonal skills, a lack of concentration, and even addictive behaviors. Furthermore, exposure to certain online environments can result in aggressive behavior. To mitigate these risks, adult supervision is crucial. Parents must implement strict usage timings and actively spread awareness about the dangers of digital addiction. By finding a balanced approach, we can harness the benefits of technology while safeguarding the holistic development of our children.

sub_questions.text_english: The student counselling department in your school put up the following poster regarding an event in the community centre. As Rita/Rahul, student editor, write a report on the above workshop for the school magazine.
sub_questions.solution: Report: Wellness Workshop at Community Centre. By Rita/Rahul. Our school's student counselling department recently organized a 'Be-Do-Live WELL' workshop at the Community Centre from February 6th to 8th. The three-day event was designed to help students navigate common concerns and foster a more balanced life. Sessions focused on practical motivation strategies and stress-reduction techniques, which were highly appreciated by the participants. The 'Theatre in Action' segment was particularly impactful, providing a creative outlet for students to express their emotions and rediscover the joy of living. The workshop succeeded in creating a supportive atmosphere where students could engage in meaningful dialogue about their mental health. Overall, the event served as a powerful reminder of the importance of emotional well-being in a student's life.

sub_questions.text_english: What does Hana ask Dr. Sadao to do alone?

options_english.B: Give him shelter in the outhouse
options_english.C: Throw him back into the sea
options_english.D: Hand him over to the authorities

sub_questions.solution: Hana is referring to Dr. Sadao's medical obligation to treat the wounded soldier on his own if necessary.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the expression: if the man were whole.

key_points: If the man was not wounded and was in good health.

sub_questions.solution: It means if the man were not wounded, Dr. Sadao would have no medical or moral excuse to treat him and would have easily handed him to the police.

sub_questions.text_english: Dr. Sadao says, All Americans are my enemy.What character trait of Dr. Sadao does it reflect?
sub_questions.solution: This reflects Dr. Sadao's patriotic commitment and his loyalty to Japan during the war.

sub_questions.text_english: Derry : I'd not come to steal anything. Mr. Lamb: No, no. The young lads steal....scrump the apples. Derry : You're not so young. I just....wanted to come in. Into the garden. Mr. Lamb: So you did. Here we are, then. Derry : You don't know who I am. Mr. Lamb: A boy. Thirteen or so. Derry : Fourteen. [Pause] But I've got to go now. Good-bye. Mr. Lamb: Nothing to be afraid of. Just a garden. Just me. Derry : But I'm not....I'm not afraid. [Pause] People are afraid of me.
Why does Mr. Lamb feel that Derry has not come to steal?

key_points: He does not react with suspicion and accepts Derry's presence peacefully.

sub_questions.solution: Mr. Lamb is not suspicious because he is an open, welcoming man who values company more than guarding his apples from a teenager.

sub_questions.text_english: Cite instances from the extract which show that Mr. Lamb is trying to put Derry at ease.

key_points: He says 'Nothing to be afraid of' and 'Just a garden. Just me'.

sub_questions.solution: Mr. Lamb tries to comfort Derry by saying 'Nothing to be afraid of' and emphasizing the simplicity of the situation by saying 'Just a garden. Just me'.

sub_questions.text_english: Choose the correct statement:

options_english.A: Derry entered the garden as he was fascinated by the bees.
options_english.B: Derry came to meet Mr. Lamb.
options_english.C: They were well acquainted with each other.
options_english.D: Derry entered as he wanted to see the garden.

sub_questions.solution: Derry explicitly states he wanted to come into the garden.

sub_questions.text_english: People are afraid of Derry because _______

fill_values: his face is scarred and distorted

sub_questions.solution: People are afraid of Derry because his facial disfigurement makes him look different and unnerving to them.

sub_questions.text_english: Children grow up in them, becoming partners in survival. And survival in Seemapuri means rag-picking. Through the years, it has acquired the proportions of a fine art. Garbage to them is gold. It is their daily bread, a roof over their heads, even if it is a leaking roof. But for a child it is even more.
Complete the sentence appropriately: Children become partners in survival suggests that _______

fill_values: the children share the burden of earning for the family at a very young age

sub_questions.solution: This suggests that the children are forced into labor early, contributing to their family's daily survival.

sub_questions.text_english: Rag-picking has acquired the proportion of a fine art means:

options_english.A: artistic bend of mind is required.
options_english.C: it has become a highly skilful activity.
options_english.D: it has discovered pieces of art.

sub_questions.solution: It means the children have become so adept and expert at rag-picking over the years that it has become a specialized skill for them.

sub_questions.text_english: State whether the given statement is True or False with reference to the extract: The children and their parents have left Dhaka to live in Seemapuri.
sub_questions.solution: The story 'Lost Spring' mentions that the people left their homes in Dhaka to settle in the outskirts of Delhi, known as Seemapuri.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does the author say 'survival in Seemapuri means rag-picking'?

key_points: Because it is the only source of income for the inhabitants.

sub_questions.solution: Rag-picking is the only means of subsistence available for the people in Seemapuri, making it essential for their survival.

sub_questions.text_english: What does the phrase for a child it is even morereveal about the children's dreams?

key_points: It represents mystery, hope, and potential for wonder.

sub_questions.solution: It reveals that for a child, garbage is not just a source of food but also a place where they hope to find hidden treasures, dreams, and joy.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following headlines suggests the central idea of the extract?

options_english.C: Art in Delhi and in Seemapuri

sub_questions.solution: The extract discusses how rag-picking is a necessity for adults and a source of wonder for children, thus offering different perspectives.

sub_questions.text_english: This settlement was adopted unanimously by the commission. Gandhi explained that the amount of the refund was less important than the fact that the landlords had been obliged to surrender part of the money and, with it, part of their prestige. Therefore, as far as the peasants were concerned, the planters had behaved as lords above the law. Now the peasant saw that he had rights and defenders. He learned courage.
What was Gandhi's purpose in agreeing to the settlement, even at a lesser amount?

key_points: To break the landlords' prestige and embolden the peasants.

sub_questions.solution: Gandhi agreed because forcing the landlords to pay a refund, regardless of the amount, effectively dismantled their aura of invincibility and empowered the peasants.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence with one word: The commission agreed by common consent, or in other words, they agreed to the settlement _______
sub_questions.solution: The settlement was adopted unanimously by the commission.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the impact on the landlords as a result of the settlement.

key_points: They lost their money and prestige.

sub_questions.solution: The settlement forced the landlords to surrender their money and, more significantly, their prestige as untouchable 'lords'.

sub_questions.text_english: Based on the content provided in the extract, select the most likely option about the behaviour of the landlords.

options_english.A: The landlords were sorry for their behaviour.
options_english.B: The landlords were obstinate and refused Gandhi's suggestion.
options_english.C: The landlords had to refund the money.
options_english.D: The landlords and the planters became partners in the Indigo plantation.

sub_questions.solution: The text states the landlords were 'obliged to surrender part of the money', meaning they had to refund it.

sub_questions.text_english: What did the peasants realize from the Champaran incident?

key_points: They had rights and defenders, and they learned courage.

sub_questions.solution: The peasants realized that they had legal rights and supporters, and more importantly, they learned the value of courage.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence appropriately: The phrase 'lords above the law' suggests that _______

fill_values: the landlords acted as though they were beyond legal accountability

sub_questions.solution: This phrase suggests the landlords behaved with absolute authority, disregarding legal fairness and treating peasants unfairly.

questions.text: Answer any five of the following six questions in 40-50 words each.

sub_questions.text_english: What was the 'thunderclap' the narrator received as M. Hamel began the lesson?
sub_questions.solution: The 'thunderclap' was M. Hamel's announcement that it was their last French lesson and that German would be taught in the schools from the next day. This news was shocking for Franz, who realized his ignorance and the permanent loss of his opportunity to learn his own language.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the sentence an army of barefoot boys who appear like the morning birds and disappear at noon.
sub_questions.solution: This metaphor describes rag-picking children who arrive in the neighborhood early in the morning, much like birds seeking food, and vanish by noon. It captures their transient existence, their poverty, and the fact that their daily cycle is centered purely on the basic necessity of survival.

sub_questions.text_english: The lesson 'The Rattrap' is both entertaining and philosophical. Do you agree with the statement? Give reasons.
sub_questions.solution: Yes, I agree. It is entertaining due to the peddler's witty observations and the ironic turn of events at the ironmaster's house. Philosophically, it explores the idea that the world is a giant rattrap, where people are lured by materialistic temptations, and kindness can spark a genuine moral transformation.

sub_questions.text_english: Bring out the contrast between Jansie and Sophie in the story 'Going Places'.
sub_questions.solution: Jansie and Sophie are complete opposites. Sophie is a dreamer who lives in an imaginary world, hoping to become famous. Jansie, conversely, is pragmatic, grounded, and cautious; she warns Sophie against her unrealistic expectations, showing that she understands the realities and limitations of their working-class life.

sub_questions.text_english: How was there a great deal of national integration in the make-up department?
sub_questions.solution: The make-up department of Gemini Studios was a prime example of national integration because it was led by a Bengali, followed by a Maharashtrian, and assisted by a Dharwar Kannadiga, an Andhra, a Madras Indian Christian, an Anglo-Burmese, and the local Tamils. They worked harmoniously, creating a unified artistic team.

sub_questions.text_english: Did Umberto Eco like to be identified as a novelist? Give reasons in support of your answer.
sub_questions.solution: No, Umberto Eco preferred to be identified as a university professor who wrote novels only on Sundays. He considered himself a scholar and academic first, viewing his novel writing as a secondary, leisure-time activity that allowed him to express ideas that his scholarly work could not.

questions.text: Answer any two of the following three questions in 40-50 words each.

sub_questions.text_english: Do you think the prediction made by the state astrologer was indisputably disproved? Give reasons in support of your answer.
sub_questions.solution: The prediction was technically fulfilled because the King did die due to a tiger, albeit a wooden one. While the King killed ninety-nine real tigers, the hundredth tiger was a toy, whose splinter caused an infection that proved fatal. Thus, the irony confirms the astrologer's prediction remained true.

sub_questions.text_english: Then I lost my spirit.What are the incidents that led Zitkala-Sa to feel this way?
sub_questions.solution: Zitkala-Sa lost her spirit after several traumatic experiences at the boarding school, including the forced cutting of her long, sacred hair, the rigid and humiliating dining rituals, and the lack of understanding from teachers. These incidents made her feel powerless, dehumanized, and separated from her cultural heritage.

sub_questions.text_english: Tishani Doshi considered the programme 'Students on Ice' a success. Do you agree with her? Why/Why not?
sub_questions.solution: Yes, I agree. The programme was a success because it allowed young students to witness the harsh realities of climate change first-hand in Antarctica. By experiencing the beauty of the ice, they were motivated to care about the planet's future, transforming from passive students into environmentally conscious individuals.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 120-150 words.

sub_questions.text_english: Franz in The Last Lessonrealizes the importance of going to school while Saheb inLost Springyearns to go to school. Write a paragraph exploring the different perspectives of these two young boys on learning and education.
sub_questions.solution: Franz and Saheb represent two contrasting perspectives on education, dictated by their circumstances. For Franz, education is a mundane, often unwelcome necessity; he frequently takes his schooling for granted, distracted by nature or his own lethargy. It is only when the privilege of learning French is snatched away that he realizes its intrinsic value and cultural significance. Conversely, for Saheb, a rag-picker, education is an unreachable dream. He yearns for the discipline and the world that a school represents, seeing it as a symbol of hope and a way out of poverty. While Franz suffers from the apathy of having too much, Saheb suffers from the deprivation of having nothing. Together, they reveal how the value of education is often judged by its availability rather than its inherent worth.

sub_questions.text_english: Write a comparative analysis for your study group focusing on how the poems Keeping Quietand My Mother at Sixty-sixilluminate the different facets of human introspection and the significance of quiet reflection in understanding oneself.
sub_questions.solution: Both 'Keeping Quiet' and 'My Mother at Sixty-six' emphasize the importance of introspection, yet they approach it from different angles. In 'Keeping Quiet', Pablo Neruda advocates for a collective, intentional silence. By stopping all activity for a moment, he suggests humanity can escape the 'sadness of never understanding ourselves', fostering global peace and a deeper connection with nature. It is a proactive, meditative act. In contrast, 'My Mother at Sixty-six' presents a more personal, emotional reflection. Kamala Das’s introspection occurs as she confronts the aging of her mother and the looming reality of death. Her quiet reflection serves as a coping mechanism, helping her reconcile her childhood fear of separation with the inevitability of change. While Neruda uses quiet to fix a broken world, Das uses it to navigate her broken heart.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 120-150 words.

sub_questions.text_english: Justify the statement, 'It may take a long time for oppression to be resisted but the seeds of rebellion are sowed early in life.'
sub_questions.solution: Oppression often leaves deep, lasting scars that may take years to yield a collective resistance, but the foundations of rebellion are indeed laid early in life through formative experiences. In 'Memories of Childhood', Zitkala-Sa’s spirit is crushed by the systemic erasure of her culture, yet the indignity she suffers fuels her resolve to resist. Similarly, the Champaran peasants in 'Indigo' endured decades of unfair sharecropping, but their capacity to resist was finally sparked by Gandhi, whose teachings validated their latent desire for justice. Early childhood experiences of injustice—be it forced assimilation or economic exploitation—create a memory of pain that later transforms into the courage to fight back. Resistance is not an overnight occurrence; it is the culmination of years of suppressed emotion finally finding a catalyst to bloom.

sub_questions.text_english: The story The Tiger Kingis a satire on the conceit of those in power. How does the author employ the literary device of dramatic irony in the story?
sub_questions.solution: The story uses dramatic irony as a powerful satirical tool to expose the foolishness of those in power. The King believes he can defy destiny and kill the hundredth tiger to ensure his immortality. The irony lies in the fact that he meticulously hunts ninety-nine real tigers, thinking he has conquered fate, while the very tool that 'kills' him—the hundredth tiger—is merely a wooden toy. The audience is aware of this destiny while the King remains blissfully ignorant of his impending death by such a trivial, ironic cause. This juxtaposition highlights the vanity of his authority; he can command nature and subjects, but he cannot command time or truth. The King’s futile efforts to prove his greatness only emphasize his smallness before the inevitability of death.
